q24968.en: Whoever is civilly obliged to pay for the damage caused by a road accident is freed from this obligation if they compensate the injured party.

explain.short: Civil liability (the duty to pay for damage) ends when the damage is paid. Once the injured person has been compensated, the debt is settled.
explain.rule: Civil liability means paying for the damage you caused. When you have paid the injured party (il danneggiato), the civil obligation is over.
explain.trap: 'si libera dall'obbligo' (is freed from the obligation) is right, but only from the duty to pay, not from any crime.

sceneParams.caption: Damage paid: the civil duty is over
lines: You caused damage: you must pay
Civil duty to pay is now over

q24969.en: Whoever is civilly obliged to pay for the damage caused by a road accident can reach an agreement with the injured party about the amount of the compensation.

explain.short: The amount to pay can be agreed between the two people. A friendly agreement is allowed; a judge is not always needed.
explain.rule: The person responsible and the injured party can agree on how much is paid (accordo). If they cannot agree, a judge decides.
explain.trap: 'può accordarsi' (can agree) is a possibility, not a duty, and it is allowed.

sceneParams.caption: You can agree the amount with the injured party
lines: You must pay for the damage
You can agree the amount together

q24970.en: Whoever is civilly obliged to pay for the damage caused by a road accident can have their own car repaired.

explain.short: Having to pay for other people's damage does not stop you from repairing your own car. Nothing forbids it.
explain.rule: The duty to pay for the damage to others is separate from your own car. You may repair your own car (at your own cost, or with an optional policy).
explain.trap: 'può far riparare il proprio autoveicolo' (can have their own car repaired): nothing forbids it, so it is true.

sceneParams.caption: You may still repair your own car
lines: You pay for the damage to others
Your own car: you can repair it

q24971.en: Whoever is civilly obliged to pay for the damage caused by a road accident can be assisted by a road-accident consultant.

explain.short: You may ask an expert for help with the accident and the compensation. This is allowed for both sides.
explain.rule: After an accident, anyone can be helped by an expert (consulente d'infortunistica stradale, a road-accident consultant), a lawyer or the insurance company.
explain.trap: 'può farsi assistere' (can be assisted) is a right, not a duty.

sceneParams.caption: You can get help from an accident expert
lines: You can ask an expert for help

q24972.en: Whoever is civilly obliged to pay for the damage caused by a road accident can, as an alternative, ask for their driving licence to be revoked.

explain.short: There is no alternative to paying for the damage. Giving up your licence does not cancel the debt.
explain.rule: Damage must be paid (by you or your insurer). A licence can be taken away only by the authorities as a penalty, never as a way to avoid paying.
explain.trap: 'in alternativa' (as an alternative): there is no alternative to paying.

sceneParams.caption: No: giving up the licence does not replace paying
lines: Revocation is a penalty, not a choice

q24973.en: Whoever is civilly obliged to pay for the damage caused by a road accident is freed from every kind of criminal liability by paying the amount of the damage.

explain.short: Paying ends only the civil duty. If a crime was committed (for example injuries), the criminal case goes on.
explain.rule: Civil liability (paying) and criminal liability (crimes, punished by the Penal Code) are separate. Money does not cancel a crime.
explain.trap: 'ogni forma di responsabilità penale' (every kind of criminal liability): paying never cancels it.

sceneParams.caption: No: paying does not cancel a crime
lines: Paying ends the civil duty only

keywords.en: by paying the amount of the damage

q24974.en: Whoever is criminally and civilly responsible for a road accident is subject to the penalties of the Penal Code.

explain.short: Criminal liability means a crime was committed. Crimes are punished with the penalties of the Penal Code (Codice Penale).
explain.rule: Criminal liability (responsabilità penale) = a crime, such as serious injuries or killing someone by accident. The Penal Code sets the punishment.
explain.trap: 'Codice Penale' (Penal Code) is not the Highway Code: crimes are punished by the Penal Code.

sceneParams.caption: Crime: penalties of the Penal Code

q24975.en: Whoever is criminally and civilly responsible for a road accident must pay compensation for the damage.

explain.short: Civil liability means you must pay for the damage. This person is civilly responsible too, so must pay.
explain.rule: Civil liability (responsabilità civile) = the duty to pay for all damage caused to people and things. The insurance (RCA) pays for you within its limits.
explain.trap: 'civilmente' (civilly) in the statement already means: must pay the damage.

sceneParams.caption: Civil liability: you must pay the damage

q24976.en: Whoever is criminally and civilly responsible for a road accident, if they broke rules of the Highway Code, is also subject to the related penalties.

explain.short: Breaking the Highway Code brings its own penalties (fines, points, licence measures). These come on top of the criminal and civil ones.
explain.rule: The three liabilities add up: criminal (Penal Code), civil (pay the damage) and administrative (Highway Code fines and points).
explain.trap: 'anche' (also): the Highway Code penalties are added, not replaced.

sceneParams.caption: Highway Code broken: its fines also apply
lines: Highway Code: fines and points too

q24977.en: Whoever is criminally and civilly responsible for a road accident may have their driving licence suspended.

explain.short: A serious accident can lead to the licence being suspended for a period. 'May' is correct: it depends on the case.
explain.rule: The person responsible for an accident can face licence measures: suspension (sospensione, for a time), revocation (revoca, taken away) or revision (revisione, a new test).
explain.trap: 'può incorrere' (may face): it is possible, not automatic.

sceneParams.caption: The licence may be suspended

q24978.en: Whoever is criminally and civilly responsible for a road accident may have their driving licence revoked.

explain.short: In the most serious cases the licence can be revoked (taken away). 'May' is correct: not in every case.
explain.rule: The person responsible for an accident can face licence measures: suspension (sospensione, for a time), revocation (revoca, taken away) or revision (revisione, a new test).
explain.trap: 'può incorrere' (may face): revocation is possible, not automatic.

sceneParams.caption: The licence may be revoked

q24979.en: Whoever is criminally and civilly responsible for a road accident may have to take the driving licence revision (a new test).

explain.short: After a serious accident, the authorities can doubt the driver's skills. They can order a revision: a new exam or medical check.
explain.rule: The person responsible for an accident can face licence measures: suspension (sospensione, for a time), revocation (revoca, taken away) or revision (revisione, a new test).
explain.trap: 'revisione' (revision) means a new test, not the car's MOT.

sceneParams.caption: The driver may have to retake the test

q24980.en: Whoever is criminally and civilly responsible for a road accident is always subject to preventive arrest.

explain.short: Arrest is not automatic after an accident. Only some very serious cases can lead to arrest.
explain.rule: Being responsible for an accident does not always mean prison or arrest. Penalties depend on the crime and are decided case by case.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) makes it false: arrest is never automatic.

sceneParams.caption: No: arrest is not automatic
lines: Arrest only in some serious cases

q24981.en: Whoever is criminally and civilly responsible for a road accident can no longer drive vehicles of the same category, but only of a lower category.

explain.short: No rule moves a driver down to a lower category. The licence can be suspended or revoked, but not 'downgraded'.
explain.rule: Licence measures are suspension, revocation or revision. There is no rule that lets you drive only smaller vehicles.
explain.trap: 'solo di categoria inferiore' (only a lower category): this measure does not exist.

sceneParams.caption: No: there is no downgrade of category

q24982.en: Whoever is criminally and civilly responsible for a road accident is in every case subject to licence revocation.

explain.short: Revocation happens only in some serious cases. It is not automatic for every accident.
explain.rule: The person responsible for an accident can face licence measures: suspension (sospensione, for a time), revocation (revoca, taken away) or revision (revisione, a new test).
explain.trap: 'in ogni caso' (in every case) makes it false: revocation is only possible.

sceneParams.caption: No: revocation is not in every case

q24983.en: Whoever is criminally and civilly responsible for a road accident is not subject to the penalties of the Highway Code.

explain.short: The Highway Code penalties still apply. They are added to the criminal and civil consequences.
explain.rule: The three liabilities add up: criminal (Penal Code), civil (pay the damage) and administrative (Highway Code fines and points).
explain.trap: 'non è assoggettato' (is not subject): wrong, the Highway Code penalties also apply.

sceneParams.caption: No: Highway Code fines still apply

q24984.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident is excluded when there is only involuntary damage to things.

explain.short: Damaging only things (cars, walls) by accident is not a crime. You must pay for it, but it is a civil matter.
explain.rule: There is no criminal liability when: only things were damaged by accident, the fact is not a crime, or there was force majeure (an event nobody could control). Paying or helping does not cancel a crime.
explain.trap: 'alle sole cose' (to things only) is the key: no people hurt, so no crime.

sceneParams.caption: Only things damaged by accident: no crime

q24985.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident is excluded when the fact is not considered a crime.

explain.short: Criminal liability exists only if there is a crime. If the law does not call the fact a crime, there is no criminal liability.
explain.rule: There is no criminal liability when: only things were damaged by accident, the fact is not a crime, or there was force majeure (an event nobody could control). Paying or helping does not cancel a crime.
explain.trap: 'non sia considerato un reato' (is not considered a crime): no crime, no criminal liability.

sceneParams.caption: Not a crime: no criminal liability

q24986.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident is excluded when the fact is due to force majeure.

explain.short: Force majeure is an event nobody could foresee or stop (for example a sudden landslide). The driver is not to blame.
explain.rule: There is no criminal liability when: only things were damaged by accident, the fact is not a crime, or there was force majeure (an event nobody could control). Paying or helping does not cancel a crime.
explain.trap: 'forza maggiore' (force majeure) = something nobody could control.

sceneParams.caption: Force majeure: no criminal liability
lines: The driver is not to blame

q24987.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident is excluded when help was given to the victim.

explain.short: Helping the victim is a duty, but it does not cancel a crime already committed.
explain.rule: There is no criminal liability when: only things were damaged by accident, the fact is not a crime, or there was force majeure (an event nobody could control). Paying or helping does not cancel a crime.
explain.trap: 'si sia prestato soccorso' (help was given): a duty, not a way out of a crime.

sceneParams.caption: No: helping does not cancel the crime
lines: Helping the victim is a duty
It does not cancel a crime
Not helping is a crime too

q24988.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident is excluded whenever the damage has been paid for.

explain.short: Paying the damage settles only the civil side. A crime is not cancelled by money.
explain.rule: There is no criminal liability when: only things were damaged by accident, the fact is not a crime, or there was force majeure (an event nobody could control). Paying or helping does not cancel a crime.
explain.trap: 'ogni qualvolta ci sia stato il risarcimento' (whenever the damage was paid): money never cancels a crime.

sceneParams.caption: No: paying does not cancel the crime

q24989.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident is excluded if the insurance company steps in and pays the injured party adequately.

explain.short: The insurance pays only the civil damage. It cannot take over a crime: criminal liability is always personal.
explain.rule: There is no criminal liability when: only things were damaged by accident, the fact is not a crime, or there was force majeure (an event nobody could control). Paying or helping does not cancel a crime.
explain.trap: 'impresa di assicurazione' (insurance company): it covers money, never crimes.

sceneParams.caption: No: insurance does not cover crimes

q24990.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident arises if it causes serious injuries to people.

explain.short: Causing serious injuries to a person in a road accident is a crime. So criminal liability arises.
explain.rule: Criminal liability arises when a crime of the Penal Code is committed, for example serious injuries or killing a person by negligence. Most Highway Code offences and damage to things only are not crimes.
explain.trap: 'lesioni gravi a persone' (serious injuries to people): this is a crime.

sceneParams.caption: Serious injuries: criminal liability

q24991.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident also arises in the case of manslaughter (killing someone by negligence).

explain.short: Killing a person by negligence (omicidio colposo) is a crime. Criminal liability arises.
explain.rule: Criminal liability arises when a crime of the Penal Code is committed, for example serious injuries or killing a person by negligence. Most Highway Code offences and damage to things only are not crimes.
explain.trap: 'omicidio colposo' = causing a death without wanting to, through carelessness.

sceneParams.caption: A death by negligence is a crime
lines: A person dies in the accident

q24992.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident arises when rules of the Penal Code are broken.

explain.short: Criminal liability means breaking the Penal Code. That is the definition of a crime.
explain.rule: Criminal liability arises when a crime of the Penal Code is committed, for example serious injuries or killing a person by negligence. Most Highway Code offences and damage to things only are not crimes.
explain.trap: 'norme contemplate dal Codice Penale' (rules of the Penal Code): exactly what makes it criminal.

sceneParams.caption: Penal Code broken: criminal liability

q24993.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident arises in every case in which the Highway Code is broken.

explain.short: Most Highway Code offences are punished with fines and points, not as crimes. Only some are crimes.
explain.rule: Criminal liability arises when a crime of the Penal Code is committed, for example serious injuries or killing a person by negligence. Most Highway Code offences and damage to things only are not crimes.
explain.trap: 'in ogni caso' (in every case) and 'Codice della strada' (Highway Code): most offences are only administrative.

sceneParams.caption: No: most Highway Code offences are fines

q24994.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident arises when the vehicle is completely destroyed.

explain.short: A destroyed vehicle is damage to things only. Damage to things by accident is not a crime.
explain.rule: Criminal liability arises when a crime of the Penal Code is committed, for example serious injuries or killing a person by negligence. Most Highway Code offences and damage to things only are not crimes.
explain.trap: 'veicolo completamente distrutto' (vehicle completely destroyed): still only damage to things.

sceneParams.caption: No: a destroyed car is damage to things

q24995.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident arises in all cases of damage to people or to things.

explain.short: Damage to things only is not a crime. So not 'all cases' bring criminal liability.
explain.rule: Criminal liability arises when a crime of the Penal Code is committed, for example serious injuries or killing a person by negligence. Most Highway Code offences and damage to things only are not crimes.
explain.trap: 'in tutti i casi' (in all cases) and 'o alle cose' (or to things): damage to things is not a crime.

sceneParams.caption: No: damage to things only is not a crime
lines: Injuries to people: may be a crime
Damage to things only: no crime

keywords.it: danni alle persone o alle cose
keywords.en: damage to people or to things

q24996.en: Criminal liability connected with a road accident falls on the owner of the vehicle if the driver has not been identified.

explain.short: Criminal liability is personal: only the person who committed the crime answers for it. The owner does not take the driver's place.
explain.rule: Criminal liability is always personal (only the driver who did it). Civil liability (paying) can fall on both driver and owner.
explain.trap: 'nei confronti del proprietario' (on the owner): a crime is never passed to another person.

sceneParams.caption: No: criminal liability is personal
lines: Crime: only the person who did it
The owner does not replace the driver

q24997.en: Civil liability connected with a road accident consists of the duty to pay for damage caused both to people and to things.

explain.short: Civil liability covers all damage: injuries to people and damage to things.
explain.rule: Civil liability is the duty to pay for every damage caused, to people and to things. It falls on the driver and the owner, it is separate from criminal and administrative liability, and the insurance pays only up to its limits (massimali).
explain.trap: 'sia alle persone che alle cose' (both to people and to things): both are covered.

sceneParams.caption: Civil liability: damage to people and things

keywords.it: sia alle persone che alle cose
keywords.en: both to people and to things

q24998.en: Civil liability connected with a road accident falls on the owner and on the driver of the vehicle.

explain.short: For paying the damage, the owner and the driver are both responsible (in solido, jointly). The injured party can ask either of them.
explain.rule: Civil liability is the duty to pay for every damage caused, to people and to things. It falls on the driver and the owner, it is separate from criminal and administrative liability, and the insurance pays only up to its limits (massimali).
explain.trap: 'proprietario e conducente' (owner and driver): civil liability falls on both.

sceneParams.caption: Civil liability: owner and driver

q24999.en: Civil liability connected with a road accident obliges the person responsible to pay for the damage.

explain.short: This is exactly what civil liability means: the responsible person pays the damage.
explain.rule: Civil liability is the duty to pay for every damage caused, to people and to things. It falls on the driver and the owner, it is separate from criminal and administrative liability, and the insurance pays only up to its limits (massimali).
explain.trap: 'obbliga ... al risarcimento' (obliges to pay): the definition of civil liability.

sceneParams.caption: Civil liability: the responsible person pays

q25000.en: Civil liability connected with a road accident is independent of criminal liability and administrative liability.

explain.short: The three liabilities are separate. You can have one, two or all three for the same accident.
explain.rule: Civil (pay the damage), criminal (crimes, Penal Code) and administrative (Highway Code fines, points) are separate and independent.
explain.trap: 'indipendente' (independent): each one follows its own rules.

sceneParams.caption: Civil, criminal, administrative: separate

q25001.en: Civil liability connected with a road accident is based on the principle that every damage caused must be paid for.

explain.short: The basic idea of civil liability: if you cause damage, you must pay for it.
explain.rule: Civil liability is the duty to pay for every damage caused, to people and to things. It falls on the driver and the owner, it is separate from criminal and administrative liability, and the insurance pays only up to its limits (massimali).
explain.trap: 'ogni danno' (every damage): the principle is general.

sceneParams.caption: Every damage caused must be paid

q25002.en: Civil liability connected with a road accident is excluded if the injured party dies.

explain.short: Death is the most serious damage. The family (heirs) has the right to be compensated.
explain.rule: Civil liability is the duty to pay for every damage caused, to people and to things. It falls on the driver and the owner, it is separate from criminal and administrative liability, and the insurance pays only up to its limits (massimali).
explain.trap: 'esclusa in caso di morte' (excluded in case of death): the opposite is true, death must also be compensated.

sceneParams.caption: No: a death must also be compensated

q25003.en: Civil liability connected with a road accident is limited to paying for damage to things only.

explain.short: Civil liability covers damage to people too, not only things.
explain.rule: Civil liability is the duty to pay for every damage caused, to people and to things. It falls on the driver and the owner, it is separate from criminal and administrative liability, and the insurance pays only up to its limits (massimali).
explain.trap: 'alle sole cose' (to things only): wrong, people are covered too.

sceneParams.caption: No: also damage to people

q25004.en: Civil liability connected with a road accident is excluded for minor damage.

explain.short: Every damage must be paid, small or big. There is no minimum.
explain.rule: Civil liability is the duty to pay for every damage caused, to people and to things. It falls on the driver and the owner, it is separate from criminal and administrative liability, and the insurance pays only up to its limits (massimali).
explain.trap: 'lieve entità' (minor): small damage must also be paid.

sceneParams.caption: No: small damage must also be paid

q25005.en: Civil liability connected with a road accident is made heavier by the lack of insurance cover.

explain.short: The damage to pay is the same with or without insurance. No insurance brings separate penalties, but does not increase the civil liability.
explain.rule: Civil liability is the duty to pay for every damage caused, to people and to things. It falls on the driver and the owner, it is separate from criminal and administrative liability, and the insurance pays only up to its limits (massimali).
explain.trap: 'aggravata' (made heavier): the amount owed does not grow; without insurance you just pay it yourself.

sceneParams.caption: No: same damage, but you pay it yourself
lines: No insurance: you pay it yourself

q25006.en: Civil liability connected with a road accident falls on the insurance company even for damage above the policy limits.

explain.short: The insurer pays only up to the limits (massimali) written in the policy. Above them, the responsible person pays.
explain.rule: Civil liability is the duty to pay for every damage caused, to people and to things. It falls on the driver and the owner, it is separate from criminal and administrative liability, and the insurance pays only up to its limits (massimali).
explain.trap: 'anche per danni superiori ai massimali' (even above the limits): the insurer stops at the limits.

sceneParams.caption: No: above the limits, you pay
lines: Insurance pays up to the limits
The responsible person pays the rest

q25007.en: The compulsory RCA insurance covers damage suffered by carried third parties (passengers) if the vehicle is authorised to carry people.

explain.short: Passengers are 'third parties' for the insurance. If the vehicle may carry people, RCA covers their injuries.
explain.rule: RCA (compulsory third-party insurance) pays for damage to other people and things on public roads, including passengers if the vehicle may carry them. Direct compensation (risarcimento diretto): your own insurer pays you, only with exactly 2 vehicles, damage to the vehicles and at most minor injuries to the drivers.
explain.trap: 'terzi trasportati' (carried third parties) = passengers: they are covered.

sceneParams.caption: RCA covers your passengers

q25008.en: The compulsory RCA insurance covers damage suffered by people and/or things that are in public areas or areas open to the public.

explain.short: RCA covers damage caused to others on public roads and in places open to the public (for example a public car park).
explain.rule: RCA (compulsory third-party insurance) pays for damage to other people and things on public roads, including passengers if the vehicle may carry them. Direct compensation (risarcimento diretto): your own insurer pays you, only with exactly 2 vehicles, damage to the vehicles and at most minor injuries to the drivers.
explain.trap: 'aree pubbliche o aperte al pubblico' (public areas or open to the public): this is where RCA applies.

sceneParams.caption: RCA: damage to others in public areas
lines: Public road or public car park

q25009.en: Direct compensation in road accidents applies if there is damage to the vehicle and minor injuries to the driver.

explain.short: Direct compensation works for damage to vehicles and for minor injuries of the drivers. Your own insurer pays you.
explain.rule: RCA (compulsory third-party insurance) pays for damage to other people and things on public roads, including passengers if the vehicle may carry them. Direct compensation (risarcimento diretto): your own insurer pays you, only with exactly 2 vehicles, damage to the vehicles and at most minor injuries to the drivers.
explain.trap: 'lesioni di lieve entità' (minor injuries): still allowed; serious injuries are not.

sceneParams.caption: Direct compensation: car damage + minor injuries

q25010.en: The direct compensation procedure cannot be used if more than two vehicles are involved.

explain.short: Direct compensation is only for accidents between exactly two vehicles. With three or more, the normal procedure is used.
explain.rule: RCA (compulsory third-party insurance) pays for damage to other people and things on public roads, including passengers if the vehicle may carry them. Direct compensation (risarcimento diretto): your own insurer pays you, only with exactly 2 vehicles, damage to the vehicles and at most minor injuries to the drivers.
explain.trap: 'più di due veicoli' (more than two vehicles): then direct compensation is not possible.

sceneParams.caption: More than 2 vehicles: no direct compensation

q25011.en: Direct compensation is excluded if a motorcycle is involved in the accident.

explain.short: A motorcycle is a normal insured vehicle. Direct compensation can be used with it too.
explain.rule: RCA (compulsory third-party insurance) pays for damage to other people and things on public roads, including passengers if the vehicle may carry them. Direct compensation (risarcimento diretto): your own insurer pays you, only with exactly 2 vehicles, damage to the vehicles and at most minor injuries to the drivers.
explain.trap: 'motociclo' (motorcycle): it does not exclude direct compensation.

sceneParams.caption: No: motorcycles can use direct compensation

q25012.en: In an accident with damage to the vehicle, the request for direct compensation must necessarily include photographs.

explain.short: Photos can help, but they are not required. The request needs the accident details, often the friendly report (CAI).
explain.rule: RCA (compulsory third-party insurance) pays for damage to other people and things on public roads, including passengers if the vehicle may carry them. Direct compensation (risarcimento diretto): your own insurer pays you, only with exactly 2 vehicles, damage to the vehicles and at most minor injuries to the drivers.
explain.trap: 'obbligatoriamente' (necessarily): photos are useful but not compulsory.

sceneParams.caption: No: photos are not compulsory
lines: Ask your own insurer to pay

q25013.en: Compulsory insurance covers damage suffered only by third parties carried in taxis.

explain.short: RCA covers passengers of any vehicle that may carry people, not only taxis.
explain.rule: RCA (compulsory third-party insurance) pays for damage to other people and things on public roads, including passengers if the vehicle may carry them. Direct compensation (risarcimento diretto): your own insurer pays you, only with exactly 2 vehicles, damage to the vehicles and at most minor injuries to the drivers.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) and 'taxi': passengers of every vehicle are covered.

sceneParams.caption: No: passengers of all vehicles are covered

q25014.en: Liability for damage connected with vehicle traffic falls on the driver and the owner of the vehicle, if it is civil liability.

explain.short: For paying damage, the driver and the owner are both responsible.
explain.rule: Civil liability (paying): driver AND owner, unless the owner proves the vehicle was used against their will (for example stolen). Criminal liability: only the driver.
explain.trap: 'responsabilità civile' (civil liability): driver and owner together.

sceneParams.caption: Civil: driver and owner

q25015.en: Liability for damage connected with vehicle traffic falls on the driver of the vehicle, if it is criminal liability.

explain.short: Criminal liability is personal: it is on the person who was driving.
explain.rule: Civil liability (paying): driver AND owner, unless the owner proves the vehicle was used against their will (for example stolen). Criminal liability: only the driver.
explain.trap: 'responsabilità penale' (criminal liability): only the driver.

sceneParams.caption: Criminal: the driver

q25016.en: Liability for damage connected with vehicle traffic does not fall on the owner of the vehicle if they prove that the vehicle was used against their will.

explain.short: If the car was stolen or used without permission, and the owner can prove it, the owner is not liable.
explain.rule: Civil liability (paying): driver AND owner, unless the owner proves the vehicle was used against their will (for example stolen). Criminal liability: only the driver.
explain.trap: 'se prova' (if they prove): the owner must prove it, for example with a theft report.

sceneParams.caption: Used against the owner's will: owner not liable
lines: Car stolen or taken without consent

q25017.en: Liability for damage connected with vehicle traffic falls on the owner of the vehicle, if it is criminal liability.

explain.short: Criminal liability is personal: only the driver who committed the crime answers for it, not the owner.
explain.rule: Civil liability (paying): driver AND owner, unless the owner proves the vehicle was used against their will (for example stolen). Criminal liability: only the driver.
explain.trap: 'proprietario' + 'responsabilità penale': the owner has only civil liability.

sceneParams.caption: No: criminal liability is only the driver's

q25018.en: Liability for damage connected with vehicle traffic falls only on the driver of the vehicle if there was damage to things.

explain.short: For damage to things, civil liability is on the driver and the owner together, not only the driver.
explain.rule: Civil liability (paying): driver AND owner, unless the owner proves the vehicle was used against their will (for example stolen). Criminal liability: only the driver.
explain.trap: 'solo del conducente' (only the driver): the owner is liable too.

sceneParams.caption: No: driver and owner both pay

q25019.en: It is forbidden to use a vehicle without insurance cover on public roads.

explain.short: RCA insurance is compulsory for every vehicle on public roads. Without it, the vehicle may not be used.
explain.rule: Without valid RCA insurance a vehicle may not be driven OR parked on public roads. The penalty is a fine and the vehicle is seized; confiscation is possible. There are no exceptions for short trips, Italy only, or paying damage yourself.
explain.trap: 'privo di copertura assicurativa' (without insurance cover): forbidden on public roads.

sceneParams.caption: No insurance: no driving on public roads

q25020.en: When the third-party car insurance has expired, you get a penalty if you drive or leave the vehicle parked on public roads.

explain.short: Both driving and parking on a public road need valid insurance. Otherwise there is a fine.
explain.rule: Without valid RCA insurance a vehicle may not be driven OR parked on public roads. The penalty is a fine and the vehicle is seized; confiscation is possible. There are no exceptions for short trips, Italy only, or paying damage yourself.
explain.trap: 'o si lascia in sosta' (or leave it parked): parking counts too.

sceneParams.caption: Expired insurance: fine for driving or parking
lines: Parked on public roads: fine too

q25021.en: When the third-party car insurance has expired, the vehicle can be confiscated.

explain.short: Besides the fine, the vehicle is seized and in some cases can be confiscated (taken by the State).
explain.rule: Without valid RCA insurance a vehicle may not be driven OR parked on public roads. The penalty is a fine and the vehicle is seized; confiscation is possible. There are no exceptions for short trips, Italy only, or paying damage yourself.
explain.trap: 'si può incorrere' (you may face): confiscation is possible.

sceneParams.caption: Expired insurance: confiscation possible

q25022.en: When the third-party car insurance has expired, you can keep using the vehicle only for short trips.

explain.short: Without valid insurance you may not drive at all, not even for a short trip.
explain.rule: Without valid RCA insurance a vehicle may not be driven OR parked on public roads. The penalty is a fine and the vehicle is seized; confiscation is possible. There are no exceptions for short trips, Italy only, or paying damage yourself.
explain.trap: 'solo per brevi tragitti' (only for short trips): no exception exists.

sceneParams.caption: No: not even short trips

q25023.en: When the third-party car insurance has expired, you can use the vehicle only in Italy.

explain.short: Expired insurance means no driving anywhere, not in Italy and not abroad.
explain.rule: Without valid RCA insurance a vehicle may not be driven OR parked on public roads. The penalty is a fine and the vehicle is seized; confiscation is possible. There are no exceptions for short trips, Italy only, or paying damage yourself.
explain.trap: 'solo sul territorio italiano' (only in Italy): it is forbidden everywhere.

sceneParams.caption: No: not in Italy either

q25024.en: When the third-party car insurance has expired, you can leave the vehicle parked on public roads.

explain.short: Parking on a public road also requires valid insurance. An uninsured car must be kept in a private place.
explain.rule: Without valid RCA insurance a vehicle may not be driven OR parked on public roads. The penalty is a fine and the vehicle is seized; confiscation is possible. There are no exceptions for short trips, Italy only, or paying damage yourself.
explain.trap: 'lasciare il veicolo in sosta' (leave it parked): parking on public roads is also forbidden.

sceneParams.caption: No: no parking on public roads

q25025.en: When the third-party car insurance has expired, the vehicle must undergo a technical test before going back on the road.

explain.short: Renewing the insurance is enough. No technical test is needed because of expired insurance.
explain.rule: Without valid RCA insurance a vehicle may not be driven OR parked on public roads. The penalty is a fine and the vehicle is seized; confiscation is possible. There are no exceptions for short trips, Italy only, or paying damage yourself.
explain.trap: 'collaudo tecnico' (technical test): not linked to insurance.

sceneParams.caption: No: just renew the insurance

q25026.en: When the third-party car insurance has expired, you can keep using the vehicle only if you are willing to pay any damage yourself.

explain.short: Insurance is compulsory by law. Being ready to pay personally does not replace it.
explain.rule: Without valid RCA insurance a vehicle may not be driven OR parked on public roads. The penalty is a fine and the vehicle is seized; confiscation is possible. There are no exceptions for short trips, Italy only, or paying damage yourself.
explain.trap: 'solo se si è disposti a pagare personalmente' (only if willing to pay yourself): not allowed.

sceneParams.caption: No: insurance is compulsory anyway

q25027.en: The "guarantee fund for road victims" pays for damage caused to people by vehicles without insurance.

explain.short: If an uninsured vehicle injures you, the guarantee fund pays instead of the missing insurance.
explain.rule: The guarantee fund for road victims pays victims hurt by vehicles that are uninsured or not identified (for example hit-and-run). It is not a pension, not a bonus and not optional.
explain.trap: 'non coperti da assicurazione' (not insured): that is the fund's job.

sceneParams.caption: Uninsured vehicle: the fund pays

q25028.en: The "guarantee fund for road victims" pays for damage caused to people by unidentified vehicles.

explain.short: If the vehicle runs away and is never found (hit-and-run), the guarantee fund pays the injured people.
explain.rule: The guarantee fund for road victims pays victims hurt by vehicles that are uninsured or not identified (for example hit-and-run). It is not a pension, not a bonus and not optional.
explain.trap: 'non identificati' (not identified): for example a hit-and-run driver.

sceneParams.caption: Unknown vehicle: the fund pays

q25029.en: The "guarantee fund for road victims" guarantees a life annuity to the injured driver.

explain.short: The fund pays damage caused by uninsured or unknown vehicles. It does not give a lifelong income to drivers.
explain.rule: The guarantee fund for road victims pays victims hurt by vehicles that are uninsured or not identified (for example hit-and-run). It is not a pension, not a bonus and not optional.
explain.trap: 'vitalizio' (life annuity): the fund gives nothing like that.

sceneParams.caption: No: the fund is not a life pension

q25030.en: The "guarantee fund for road victims" is a reward for those who have not caused accidents.

explain.short: The fund helps victims, it is not a bonus for good drivers.
explain.rule: The guarantee fund for road victims pays victims hurt by vehicles that are uninsured or not identified (for example hit-and-run). It is not a pension, not a bonus and not optional.
explain.trap: 'premio' (reward): the fund is for victims, not a prize.

sceneParams.caption: No: the fund is for victims, not a prize
lines: Not a bonus for good drivers

q25031.en: The "guarantee fund for road victims" is an optional agreement.

explain.short: The fund is set up by law and works for every victim. Nobody chooses to join it.
explain.rule: The guarantee fund for road victims pays victims hurt by vehicles that are uninsured or not identified (for example hit-and-run). It is not a pension, not a bonus and not optional.
explain.trap: 'facoltativa' (optional): the fund is provided by law.

sceneParams.caption: No: the fund is set by law

q25032.en: The "guarantee fund for road victims" pays for damage caused by drivers who are minors.

explain.short: Being a minor is not a case for the fund. The fund steps in for uninsured or unidentified vehicles.
explain.rule: The guarantee fund for road victims pays victims hurt by vehicles that are uninsured or not identified (for example hit-and-run). It is not a pension, not a bonus and not optional.
explain.trap: 'conducenti minorenni' (minor drivers): not a case covered by the fund.

sceneParams.caption: No: minors are not the fund's case

q25033.en: Insurance policies usually taken out to cover theft, fire, vandalism, natural events or damage to your own vehicle (kasko policy) are not compulsory.

explain.short: Only RCA is compulsory. All the other policies are a free choice.
explain.rule: Only RCA is compulsory. Policies for theft, fire, vandalism, natural events or your own car damage (kasko) are optional. Theft/fire pay at most the vehicle's value at that moment, cover accidental fires too, and need no special devices.
explain.trap: 'non sono obbligatorie' (are not compulsory): correct, they are optional.

sceneParams.caption: Theft, fire, kasko: optional

q25034.en: In an insurance policy against theft or fire, the compensation due cannot be higher than the value the vehicle had when it was stolen or caught fire.

explain.short: Insurance repays the loss, it does not make you richer. You get at most what the car was worth at that moment.
explain.rule: Only RCA is compulsory. Policies for theft, fire, vandalism, natural events or your own car damage (kasko) are optional. Theft/fire pay at most the vehicle's value at that moment, cover accidental fires too, and need no special devices.
explain.trap: 'al momento' (at the moment): the value when stolen or burned, not the new price.

sceneParams.caption: Paid at most the car's value at that time

q25035.en: If the vehicle is stolen in a foreign country, to activate the insurance you must repeat the theft report in Italy.

explain.short: The Italian insurer needs an Italian police report. So a theft reported abroad must be reported again in Italy.
explain.rule: Only RCA is compulsory. Policies for theft, fire, vandalism, natural events or your own car damage (kasko) are optional. Theft/fire pay at most the vehicle's value at that moment, cover accidental fires too, and need no special devices.
explain.trap: 'ripetere la denuncia' (repeat the report): the report must be made again in Italy.

sceneParams.caption: Theft abroad: report it again in Italy

q25036.en: The insurance policy against theft or fire guarantees a life annuity to the vehicle owner if the vehicle is stolen or catches fire.

explain.short: The policy pays once, at most the value of the vehicle. It is not a lifelong income.
explain.rule: Only RCA is compulsory. Policies for theft, fire, vandalism, natural events or your own car damage (kasko) are optional. Theft/fire pay at most the vehicle's value at that moment, cover accidental fires too, and need no special devices.
explain.trap: 'rendita vitalizia' (life annuity): the policy pays only the vehicle's value.

sceneParams.caption: No: it pays the car's value, not a pension

q25037.en: To take out an insurance policy against fire, the vehicle must have a special automatic battery-disconnect device.

explain.short: No special device is required to buy a fire policy.
explain.rule: Only RCA is compulsory. Policies for theft, fire, vandalism, natural events or your own car damage (kasko) are optional. Theft/fire pay at most the vehicle's value at that moment, cover accidental fires too, and need no special devices.
explain.trap: 'occorre' (it is necessary): no device is required.

sceneParams.caption: No: no special device needed

q25038.en: To take out an insurance policy against theft, the vehicle must have an anti-theft device.

explain.short: An alarm can lower the price, but it is not required to buy a theft policy.
explain.rule: Only RCA is compulsory. Policies for theft, fire, vandalism, natural events or your own car damage (kasko) are optional. Theft/fire pay at most the vehicle's value at that moment, cover accidental fires too, and need no special devices.
explain.trap: 'occorre' (it is necessary): an anti-theft device is not required.

sceneParams.caption: No: anti-theft device not required

q25039.en: Insurance policies against vehicle fire normally cover only damage from deliberate (intentional) fires and not from accidental fires.

explain.short: A fire policy normally covers accidental fires too, for example an electrical fault.
explain.rule: Only RCA is compulsory. Policies for theft, fire, vandalism, natural events or your own car damage (kasko) are optional. Theft/fire pay at most the vehicle's value at that moment, cover accidental fires too, and need no special devices.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) and 'dolosi' (deliberate): accidental fires are covered too.

sceneParams.caption: No: accidental fires are covered too
